newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-UNCONFIRMED REPORTS SAY MESSIER GOING TO VANCOUVER.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-UNCONFIRMED REPORTS SAY MESSIER GOING TO VANCOUVER.

text.p: Unconfirmed reports were flying Sunday night saying that free agent centre Mark Messier, who led the Rangers to the Stanley Cup in 1994, was spurning New York to sign an extremely lucrative three-year contract with the Vancouver Canucks.
The ESPN cable television network and local broadcast reports have cited unidentified sources and variously put the deal at $18 million (U.S.) to $20 million for three years.
A spokesman for the Canucks told Reuters there was no press conference scheduled for Monday but there would be a clarification of their offer.
"There will be an announcement Monday clarifying our offer to Messier," said Steve Tambellini, Canucks public relations director. "That's all I'm going to say to you."
Rangers spokesmen said they knew nothing about the reports concerning their team captain.
Messier was vacationing in Hilton Head Island, South Carolina.

The 36-year-old Messier had 36 goals and 48 assists last season in the final year of a three-year, $18 million contract with the Rangers. He led New York to its first Stanley Cup in 54 years in 1994, earning his sixth career Stanley Cup ring.

Various reports have said the Rangers offered a two-year, $10 million offer to Messier, though there has also been speculation that losing him could benefit the club politically by giving full control of the team to coach Colin Campbell, who received a contract extension earlier this month.

The Canucks, who lost last year's bidding war for Wayne Gretzky to New York, could consider Messier a good candidate to help get the most out of inconsistent star Russian wingers Pavel Bure and Alexander Mogilny,.
With Messier aboard, they could boast two top lines also including Bure, Mogilny and the current team captain, Trevor Linden.
The Canucks missed the playoffs last season by going 35-40-7 for 77 points. They also had trouble filling GM Place, their new arena.

Messier revealed last week that he had narrowed his choice as an unrestricted free agent to five "very interested" teams. The others in the running were believed to be the Washington Capitals, the Edmonton Oilers and the Detroit Red Wings.

In 18 NHL seasons with Edmonton and the Rangers, Messier is 10th all-time in goals with 575, sixth in assists with 977 and fifth in points with 1,552. Messier won the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff Most Valuable Player for the Oilers in 1984. He also won the Hart Trophy, given to the league's MVP, in 1990 with Edmonton and 1992 with the Rangers.
Messier teamed with Gretzky on the Oilers dynasty of the 1980s, but also led Edmonton to the 1990 Stanley Cup after Gretzky's departure.

Though he suffered through one of the worst playoff performances of his career, scoring three goals with nine assists in 15 games, Messier is still second to Gretzky among all-time post-season performers with 109 goals, 186 assists and 295 points.

Messier led the Rangers to the Stanley Cup less than three years after joining the team. He broke what many fans deemed "The Curse" and came through despite the pressure of being hailed as the saviour of the franchise.

En route to the Cup in the 1994 Eastern Conference finals, Messier, with the Rangers trailing three games to two, guaranteed a victory in Game 6 in New Jersey and had a natural hat trick in the third period to ensure the win. The Rangers won the seventh game in double overtime and went on to defeat the Canucks in seven games to win the Cup.
